title: Sell the ghosts by night and keep the haunted wing free by day
paragraphs: Hollowmere's haunted wing attracted 41,000 visitors last year, and the trustees naturally want their share of the takings. So what should they charge for: the doorway, or the darkness?

A £5 admission charge looks simplest. October's pilot weekend halved attendance, yet the remaining 20,500 paying visitors would still contribute £102,500 a year, before counting what the library loses.
But ghost-hunters are enthusiastic borrowers. Six in ten leave carrying a book, the council reimburses the library £2.10 per loan, and halving the crowd costs £26,250 of that grant.
The ghost, meanwhile, keeps library opening hours in reverse. The Grey Archivist appears after closing time in nine sightings out of ten, precisely when nobody is paying a penny.
So sell what daytime visitors never witness: a £22 after-dark tour. Thirty places, four evenings weekly across 50 weeks, gives 6,000 places; at 90% occupancy, £118,800 a year.
The tour leaves the free wing, its 25,000 loans and the council's grant precisely where they are, and requires two volunteer guides, steady nerves and generous supplies of torches.

panel.text: Keep the haunted wing free and sell a £22 after-dark tour: 30 places, four nights a week. At 90% full it earns £118,800 a year; a £5 door charge nets £76,250 and costs the library half its loans.

title: Gearpaw should open a firmware hotline before it builds a second repair bay
highlight: 8,200 visits a year off the bench

paragraphs.lead: Most robot pets are not broken
paragraphs.text: Of Gearpaw's 18,400 visits in 2026, 64% were firmware faults: a dog that fetches the wrong slipper, a cat stuck in a purr loop, a parrot that only speaks in error codes. Only 36% needed a spanner.

paragraphs.lead: A second bay treats the wrong patient
paragraphs.text: The £480,000 bay adds 5,200 bench visits a year, yet most of them would go to firmware faults that occupy a welder's bench for 22 minutes and never need a welding torch.

paragraphs.lead: A hotline fixes pets where they sleep
paragraphs.text: Remote diagnostics clear seven in ten firmware faults in 9 minutes over the owner's home network, with no carry case in sight. That takes 8,200 visits a year off the bench for £120,000.
With firmware off the bench, the wait for a slot drops from 11 days to 4, and the three welders spend their shifts on hips, tails and hinges, not resets.
Mechanical cases grow about 15% a year, so the bench fills up again around 2030. That is the year to build the second bay, when there is real welding to put in it.

panel.text: A £120,000-a-year hotline frees 8,200 bench visits, while a £480,000 second bay adds only 5,200. The hotline also cuts the wait for a bench slot from 11 days to 4.

title: The volcano heats the springs for free, and they earn 48% of revenue
subtitle: Spa revenue by treatment line, FY26, €20m in total
pointsHeading: What each line costs to run

points.text: The crater springs earn €9.6m of the €20m and need no boiler: the volcano does all the heating.
Mud baths add €5.4m; the mud is dug on site, so their margin is nearly as fat as the springs'.
Lava-stone massage brings in €3.6m but needs 40 trained therapists, the largest single payroll line in the resort.
Ash facials earn only €1.4m, and the salon has to close for the day every time the mountain coughs.
Together the two lines the volcano powers, springs and mud, bring in €15m, three quarters of the total.

title: Cocktail bars buy 46% of all artisanal ice, and they want it round
subtitle: Spend on artisanal ice by buyer and cube type, 2026, €100m in total

points.text: Spheres are 57% of what cocktail bars spend on ice, and the bars buy two thirds of every sphere sold. They pay €2 a sphere because it melts slowly.
Fine dining and hotels spend €39m between them, mostly on clear cubes for water and wine buckets. They buy on reliability of delivery, not on shape.
Home bartenders spend only €10m, but 40% of it on flavoured cubes, a line the bars barely touch. That is a supermarket product, not a bar one.

title: Eight in ten residents could outrun a zombie; only two have a plan to regroup
subtitle: Residents out of ten meeting each readiness test, Manchester survey of 2,000, 2026

points.text: Fitness is not the gap: eight in ten can already outrun a slow zombie over 100 metres.
Only three in ten know their nearest high ground, so signpost the hills before buying anything.
Two in ten have a regroup plan; a fridge-magnet plan card costs us 12p a household.
Food is the dearest fix: three days of tins in every home would cost us £4m in all.
